study_identification_part.si_4_title: Accommodating Site Variation In Neuroimaging Data Using Normative And Hierarchical Bayesian Models

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: The study proposes and compares two hierarchical Bayesian models for normative modeling: (1) Hierarchical Bayesian Linear Model (HBLM) - a linear regression model with site as a random effect, and (2) Hierarchical Bayesian Gaussian Process Model (HBGPM) - a non-linear model using Gaussian Process to capture non-linear age effects with site as a random effect. Both models were implemented in Stan and use partial pooling across sites via shared priors.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: Our normative hierarchical Bayesian models (both the linear HBLM and non-linear HBGPM versions), explicitly modeling site effects within the normative modeling framework, outperformed all alternative harmonization models; The Stan code for the HBLM, the HBGPM and the simple Bayesian linear model without site as predictor can be found at https://github.com/likeajumprope/Bayesian_normative_models
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: Bayer2022.pdf.md: Section 5 Discussion / Section 3.8 Model specification

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: The study modeled cortical thickness from structural MRI as the response variable. Specifically, 35 cortical thickness measures (regions) from the Desikan-Killiany atlas were used, derived from FreeSurfer processing of the ABIDE dataset.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: We compared the performance of a linear and a non-linear hierarchical Bayesian model in modeling the effect of age on cortical thickness; measures of cortical thickness (Fortin et al., 2018); cortical thickness can be non-linear

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age was used as the primary predictor (fixed effect) for modeling cortical thickness trajectories. In the HBGPM model, age was modeled non-linearly using a Gaussian Process. Sex was included as a covariate in the models to preserve biological variation of interest. Site was included as a random effect in the hierarchical Bayesian models to account for scanner/acquisition differences across the 17 sites in the ABIDE dataset.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: We compared the performance of a linear and a non-linear hierarchical Bayesian model in modeling the effect of age on cortical thickness; An overview of the distribution of age and sex for the training and test sets for healthy controls and individuals with autism can be found in Fig. 2; The ability of the model to deal with site effects is obtained by introducing a random effect for site s = 1, 2, . . . ,q so that the prediction for the i th subject is a combination of fixed and varying effects; We propose a hierarchical Bayesian approach in which we include site as a random effect in the model
